NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A festival where everyone sings, however badly: hold it, or fear the elders' ears.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has proposed a festival where everyone must sing, no matter how terrible their voice. (friend) has a famously awful voice and is horrified. The elders are worried about their ears. The children have already started planning a prank involving a giant fake fish. What should happen?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The festival is glorious and dreadful. (friend) sings a solo that sends the birds out of the trees, and gets the biggest cheer of the night. The children's giant fish is upstaged by the elders, who arrive dressed as a whale.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The festival is held on the far beach, far from the elders' huts. The elders come anyway, and hold a storytelling duel about who has heard the worst singing. The children's fish prank goes perfectly.
